info.description: Read calls, contacts, appointments and messages, book appointments, and subscribe to webhooks. Authenticate with an API key in the Authorization header. A platform key also names the business it acts on in the LobbyStack-Business header. Each key allows 120 requests per minute by default.

post.description: Platform keys only. A host's key creates a business owned by the account in the key's owner_email, and lets every key in the same group act on it. A partner's key creates a business of the partner with no owner yet, at the access_level you pick, and the partner emails owner_email an invitation to own it. With a partner's key, template_id also needs partner:read and package_id also needs partner.businesses:write. Idempotency-Key is required: a retry with the same value returns the business it created, however much later, and a different body with that value is a 422.

post.summary: Invite an owner to make an account
post.description: Platform keys only. Emails the address a link to sign up, so an owner with no LobbyStack account can make one and then accept your claim link. With a partner's key, the email comes from the partner and links to its dashboard. If the address already has an account, LobbyStack emails it a link to sign in instead and changes nothing. The answer is the same either way, so it never tells you whether someone has an account. No account exists until the person signs up, with a password or with Google. Idempotency-Key is required: a retry of the same request sends nothing more. One platform key can invite 50 addresses a day, and a partner's platform keys can invite 50 between them; past that the key gets a 429.

The account a key acts as can search 20 times in 10 minutes; searches refused before that don't count. Send replaces to find a replacement for an active number; a business can replace its number once.

post.description: Buys the offered number for the business and connects it to the receptionist. It costs money, so Idempotency-Key is required. Returns the claim at once; poll GET /phone-numbers/claims/{claim_id} until its status is claimed or failed. A business that already has a number, including one still being released, or another claim in progress gets a 409. Claims are limited to 3 an hour, 2 a day and 5 in 30 days, past which they are a 429. Platform keys count each business's claims; other keys count the claims of the account they act as. A partner's businesses also share daily and 30-day limits, whichever key claims. They buy up to the larger of 2 and the numbers the partner's tier includes a day, and the larger of 5 and twice those in 30 days. A trial offer starts the business's 14-day free trial. As in the dashboard, each business, account and verified phone gets one trial. The dashboard also allows one trial per network in 30 days, and the API doesn't: an integration claims for all of its customers from the same addresses.
